_about: Deliverance side by side (plan 7.6b): wordings of deliverance and salvation that more than one book shares, from the Exodus and the history books to the psalms, the prophets, the Gospels and the letters, with what is alike and what differs. Every quotation machine-checked against the Berean; rows chosen and drafted by Claude Opus from the passages the theme map cites, the Berean editors' quotation notes and a search of the whole Berean; widened by the completeness search; every Alike and Different line read by the nine-reader panel (Sonnet). Takes no interpretive stance. A cell [verse, words, "aside"] is off the subject and shown, with an asterisk, for its shared words.
columns_note: The Law & history: Genesis to Esther. Psalms & wisdom: Job to the Song of Solomon. The Prophets: Isaiah to Malachi.

rows.alike: The LORD fights for His people: "The LORD will fight for you" (Exodus 14:14), "the LORD your God Himself will fight for you" (Deuteronomy 3:22), "Our God will fight for us!" (Nehemiah 4:20), "the LORD fought for Israel" (Joshua 10:14), "the battle is the LORD's" (1 Samuel 17:47).
rows.different: Exodus 14:13-14 has "Stand firm and you will see the LORD's salvation" and "you need only to be still"; 2 Chronicles 20:17 has "You need not fight this battle. Take up your positions, stand firm, and see the salvation of the LORD on your behalf", and 20:15 "the battle does not belong to you, but to God". Deuteronomy 20:4 has the LORD going "to fight for you against your enemies, to give you the victory", and 2 Chronicles 32:8 "with us is the LORD our God to help us and to fight our battles". Joshua 23:3 says it in the past, "it was the LORD your God who fought for you", and 23:10 "the LORD your God fights for you, just as He promised". Psalm 35:1 asks it in prayer, "fight against those who fight against me"; Jeremiah 21:5 has "I Myself will fight against you", and Zechariah 14:3 "the LORD will go out to fight against those nations".

rows.different: In Ezekiel 20:33-34 the strong hand and outstretched arm come with "outpoured wrath", and Jeremiah 21:5 has "with an outstretched hand and a mighty arm" where the LORD says "I Myself will fight against you". 1 Kings 8:42 has "they will hear of Your great name and mighty hand and outstretched arm" of one who "comes and prays toward this temple", and 2 Chronicles 6:32 has "Your great name and Your mighty hand and outstretched arm" of "the foreigner who is not of Your people Israel"; Jeremiah 27:5 uses "outstretched arm" of making the earth: "By My great power and outstretched arm, I made the earth". rows.alike: The bringing out of Egypt is named again and again: "I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt" (Exodus 20:2), "I am the LORD your God, who brought you up out of Egypt" (Psalm 81:10), "I brought you up from the land of Egypt" (Amos 2:10), "to lead them out of the land of Egypt" (Hebrews 8:9), "who brought you out of the land of Egypt" (Deuteronomy 13:5, 13:10), "I brought you up out of Egypt" (Judges 2:1, 6:8).
rows.different: Deuteronomy 4:20 and Jeremiah 11:4 add "out of the iron furnace", and 1 Kings 8:51 "out of the furnace for iron". Exodus 29:46 adds "so that I might dwell among them", and Leviticus 25:38 "to give you the land of Canaan". Deuteronomy 6:12 warns "be careful not to forget the LORD who brought you out of the land of Egypt"; Judges 2:12 has "they forsook the LORD, the God of their fathers, who had brought them out of the land of Egypt", and 1 Kings 9:9 "they have forsaken the LORD their God who brought their fathers out of the land of Egypt". Numbers 21:5 asks, against God and against Moses, "Why have you led us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness?", and Deuteronomy 1:27 has "Because the LORD hates us, He has brought us out of the land of Egypt"; Jeremiah 16:14 says "they will no longer say" it, and Amos 9:7 sets beside it "the Philistines from Caphtor, and the Arameans from Kir". Hosea 12:13 says "by a prophet", Hebrews 3:16 "those Moses led out of Egypt", and Jude 1:5 "Jesus had delivered His people out of the land of Egypt". Exodus 13:3 has "by the strength of His hand", and Numbers 16:13 has "brought us up out of a land flowing with milk and honey to kill us in the wilderness".

(1 Kings 12:28, "two golden calves"), and the like words of Moses, "As for this Moses who brought us up out of the land of Egypt" (Exodus 32:1), "As for this Moses who led us out of the land of Egypt" (Acts 7:40).

(2 Kings 18:33, Isaiah 36:18), "Have the gods of these nations ever been able to deliver their land from my hand?" (2 Chronicles 32:13), "Then what god will be able to deliver you from my hands?" Mark 16:16 has "Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, but whoever does not believe will be condemned"; Romans 10:10 has "with your mouth you confess and are saved"; 1 Corinthians 15:2 has "By this gospel you are saved, if you hold firmly to the word I preached to you. Otherwise, you have believed in vain."; Acts 16:31 continues "you and your household".
